docs.title: droid
docs.text:
droid enables Detection as Code using Sigma. Keep your detection rules as Sigma in a Git repository, and droid validates them, converts them for each of your platforms, searches your logs with them and deploys them to your SIEM and EDR, from your laptop or your CI/CD pipeline.

Built on pySigma, droid also handles rules written directly in a platform's query language, the raw rules.

  • Set up in minutes

    Install detect-droid with pip, add the pySigma backends of your platforms, and convert your first rules.

    Getting started

  • Detection as Code

    Review, version and roll back your detection rules like code, and let your CI/CD pipeline test and deploy them.

    Usage

  • Made to measure

    Map each log source to your data with its own pipelines, and tune schedules, suppression and actions per platform, log source or rule.

    Configuration

  • Open source, EUPL

    droid is licensed under the EUPL and developed in the open on GitHub.

    License

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Validate the syntax and the quality of your Sigma rules with the pySigma validators
  • Convert them for each platform, with the pipelines you set per log source
  • Search your logs with them, and report the hits before going live
  • Export them to your platforms: create, update, disable and remove detection rules
  • Check the integrity of what runs on a platform against your repository
  • Correlate with Sigma correlation rules
  • Serve one log source from several telemetry sources, each converted with its own pipelines, see Log source variants
  • Manage several tenants (MSSP) with per customer filters
  • Update your rules from upstream sources such as SigmaHQ

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
Platform --platform Search Export Integrity Rule actions MSSP Splunk splunk ✅ ✅ ✅ Email, webhook Microsoft Sentinel microsoft_sentinel ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Microsoft Defender XDR microsoft_xdr ✅ ✅ ✅ Response actions on users, files and devices ✅ Elastic Security (ES|QL) esql ✅ ✅ ✅ Index, server log, email, webhook Elastic Security (EQL) eql ✅ ✅ ✅ Index, server log, email, webhook Info

Each platform needs its pySigma backend, see Getting started. Your platform is missing? Contributions are welcome.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
droid rules validate  -r sigma-rules/ -c droid_config.toml              # check your rules
droid rules convert   -r sigma-rules/ -c droid_config.toml -p splunk    # see the queries they become
droid rules search    -r sigma-rules/ -c droid_config.toml -p splunk    # search your logs with them
droid rules export    -r sigma-rules/ -c droid_config.toml -p splunk    # deploy them
droid rules integrity -r sigma-rules/ -c droid_config.toml -p splunk    # check what runs on the platform

docs.title: Configure droid
docs.text:
The tool is flexible and requires a TOML (.toml) configuration file for various tasks. If you have cloned the example repository, just open droid_config.toml.

The next sections will highlight the config per sections.

docs.title: Configure the basics
docs.text:
[base]

raw_rules_directory = "rules/raw" # (1)!

sigma_validation_config = "validation/validate.yml" # (2)!

sigma_filters_directory = "filters/" # (3)!
...

  1. This is the location of the raw rules directory.

  2. This is the location of the Sigma validation config. See the appropriate section below.

  3. Optional. This is the location of the Sigma filters rules.

docs.title: Configure the platform
docs.text:
Next, configure your platform in the platforms section. You will find in one of the platforms page the required parameters.

[platforms.supported_platform]

...
Warning

Make sure your platform is supported here.

docs.title: Configure your plaform pipelines
docs.text:
droid ease the conversion of the Sigma rules for the desired platform by leveraging the Sigma pipelines. It applies the platforms you desire by log sources.

droid will look for a match with the Sigma logsource fields and the platform pipelines config.

proc_access_win_svchost_credential_dumping.yml
title: Credential Dumping Attempt Via Svchost
id: 174afcfa-6e40-4ae9-af64-496546389294
status: test
description: Detects when a process tries to access the memory of svchost to potentially dump credentials.
references:
    - Internal Research
author: Florent Labouyrie
date: 2021/04/30
modified: 2022/10/09
tags:
    - attack.t1548
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_access
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\svchost.exe'
        GrantedAccess: '0x143a'
    filter_main_known_processes:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\msiexec.exe'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: high
droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_access]

pipelines = ["pipelines/splunk_process_access.yml", "splunk_windows"]
product = "windows"
category = "process_access"

In the above example, when the Sigma logsource product and category of the Sigma rules will match the configuration platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_access, the Sigma pipelines will be loaded:

  • splunk_windows is part of the pySigma Splunk backend
  • pipelines/splunk_process_access.yml is a custom pipeline to apply the necessary transforms
Info

Make sure to install the appropriate pySigma backend for the supported platform. See the installation section.

splunk_process_access.yml
name: Splunk Windows process access
priority: 100

# Author: Mathieu LE CLEACH
# Purpose if this pipeline:
# Process the windows/process_access rules in Splunk

transformations:
  - id: index_condition
    type: add_condition
    conditions:
      index: windows_sysmon
      splunk_server: "*prod.planet-express.local"
    rule_conditions:
      - type: logsource
        category: process_access
        product: windows

postprocessing:
- type: template
  template: |+
    {{ query }} | table _time,host,user,SourceImage,TargetImage,CallTrace,GrantedAccess
Info

If droid does not find a match, it will process the Sigma rule as "non-configured" since the log sources was not configured for the given platform. For the purpose of the automation through CI/CD pipelines, droid will not issue an error exit-code for non-configured log sources.

docs.title: Correlation rule overrides
docs.text:
Some backend formats are incompatible with Sigma correlation rules. For these cases, the [platforms.<backend>.pipelines.<group>] section accepts two optional fields that override the pipelines and the output format only when the rule file is a correlation rule:

  • pipelines_correlation (list of strings): overrides pipelines for correlation rules.
  • format_correlation (string): overrides format for correlation rules.

Both fields are optional and additive. Atomic rules in the same group are unaffected.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_creation]

pipelines = ["splunk_windows", "pipelines/splunk_process_creation.yml"]
pipelines_correlation = ["splunk_windows"] # (1)!
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"
format = "data_model"
format_correlation = "default" # (2)!

  1. Correlation rules in this group fall back to the bare backend pipeline.

  2. Correlation rules in this group are emitted as default SPL instead of data_model.

In the example above, atomic rules convert to data-model SPL while correlation rules in the same log source group fall back to the bare backend pipeline and default SPL.

Resolution semantics

For a given rule, the effective pipelines and format are resolved as follows:

Effective pipelines:

  • correlation rule and pipelines_correlation set → pipelines_correlation
  • otherwise → pipelines

Effective format:

  • correlation rule and format_correlation set → format_correlation
  • else if format set → format
  • else → "default"

A rule file is treated as a correlation rule if any YAML document in the file has a top-level correlation: key.

docs.title: Log source variants
docs.text:
A log source can be served by more than one telemetry source, for instance Sysmon and a third-party EDR for windows/process_creation. Declare one pipeline group per source, give each a variant name and mark one of them primary, and droid will convert and deploy one query per source.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_creation]

pipelines = ["splunk_windows", "pipelines/splunk_process_creation.yml"]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"
variant = "sysmon"
primary = true

See the log source variants page for the identity rules, the per-platform and per-customer selection, and the Splunk specifics.

docs.title: Configure the validation
docs.text:
You can validate the Sigma rules on the syntax level by leveraging the pySigma rule validation. It requires a validation configuration file that can be placed in your repository.

validate.yml
validators:
    - all
    - -tlpv1_tag
    - -escaped_wildcard
Note

Make sure to provide the path to your droid configuration.

docs.title: Rule custom fields
docs.text:
You can place custom fields in your rules to:

  • Disable a rule: disabled: True
  • Remove a rule: removed: True

Additionally:

  • ignore_search to True will skip the search step
  • ignore_export_error to True will ignore the export error and integrity error
Info

The ignore_export_error option currently only works with raw detection rules.

Some of the settings placed in your droid configuration file can be replaced as well.

example_sigma.yml
title: Load Undocumented Autoelevated COM Interface
id: fb3722e4-1a06-46b6-b772-253e2e7db933
status: test
description: COM interface (EditionUpgradeManager) that is not used by standard executables.
references:
    - https://www.snip2code.com/Snippet/4397378/UAC-bypass-using-EditionUpgradeManager-C/
    - https://gist.github.com/hfiref0x/de9c83966623236f5ebf8d9ae2407611
author: oscd.community, Dmitry Uchakin
date: 2020/10/07
modified: 2021/11/27
tags:
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1548.002
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|contains: 'EXCEL.EXE'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: high
custom:
    #ignore_search: True
    disabled: True
    #removed: True
    #ignore_export_error: True
    earliest_time: -1h@h
    latest_time: now
    cron_schedule: '5 * * * *'
    alert.suppress: "0"
    #alert.suppress.fields: "customer,host,user"
    alert.digest_mode: "1"
    actions: "webhook"
    action.webhook.param.url: "https://automation.pizza-planet.local/34432/44232"

You can also replace the webhook URL at the rule level by using action.webhook.param.url: "$WEBHOOK_URL_SOMETHING".

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
droid is published as a Python package and can be installed with pip in a virtual environment or in a Docker container. The installation is straightforward:

  • Install droid and the desired Sigma backends and pipelines
  • Configure your droid configuration file
  • Configure your Sigma pipelines
  • Optional: Validate your rules using pySigma validators

If you already have a repository containing all your Sigma rules or if you wish to start from scratch we made available a repository to start with droid by cloning it.

docs.title: Install droid
docs.text:
1. Open up a terminal and install droid with:
Latest0.3.X 
pip install detect-droid

pip install detect-droid=="0.3.X"

docs.title: Install the Sigma backends
docs.text:
Install the backend of each platform you target, in these versions:

pip install pysigma-backend-splunk==2.1.0          # Splunk
pip install pysigma-backend-kusto==1.0.1           # Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR
pip install pysigma-backend-elasticsearch==2.1.1   # Elastic Security
Warning

Keep these versions: they support the pySigma version droid relies on. The latest releases of some backends require a newer pySigma and upgrade it, which breaks the other backends.

Note

You will find the full list of backends on the Sigma documentation page.

docs.title: Install additional Sigma pipelines
docs.text:
This is optional but you can install additional pipelines. For instance:

pip install pysigma-pipeline-windows # (1)!
  1. Windows logsource to Channel field and generic logsource to Windows audit events mapping
Note

You will find the full list of pipelines on the Sigma documentation page. Select "Pipelines" from "Plugin Type".

docs.title: Log source variants
docs.text:
A Sigma log source names the kind of telemetry a rule needs, not where that telemetry comes from. windows/process_creation usually means Sysmon EventCode 1, but the same detection is just as valid over the process events of a third-party EDR. webserver usually means the Azure WAF logs, but some workspaces carry AGWAccessLogs instead.

A variant is one telemetry source serving one log source. Each variant has its own pipeline group, produces its own query, and is deployed as its own object on the platform.

Info

Variants are entirely optional. A log source served by a single pipeline group needs no variant key at all, and every configuration written before this feature existed keeps behaving exactly as it did.

docs.title: Declaring variants
docs.text:
Variants are declared by adding variant to the pipeline groups that serve the same log source, and by marking exactly one of them primary.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_creation]

pipelines = ["splunk_windows", "pipelines/splunk_process_creation.yml"]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"
variant = "sysmon" # (1)!
primary = true # (2)!

[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_creation_edr]

pipelines = ["splunk_windows", "pipelines/splunk_process_creation_edr.yml"]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"
variant = "edr" # (3)!

  1. The name of the telemetry source. It is used to derive the rule identity and to select the variant per platform or per customer.

  2. Exactly one group per log source must claim the primary role. It keeps the bare Sigma id and the bare rule title.

  3. No primary key, so this group deploys under a derived identity.

Rules matching windows/process_creation now convert twice, once through each pipeline group. The Sysmon pipeline points at the Sysmon index, the EDR pipeline points at the EDR one, and both queries are deployed.

docs.title: Configuration errors
docs.text:
Once a log source is served by more than one group, droid refuses to guess and raises an error when:

  • one of the groups has no variant name
  • two groups declare the same variant name
  • no group, or more than one group, claims primary
Warning

Before variants existed, two pipeline groups matching the same log source silently resolved to whichever one the configuration happened to list first. That coin flip is now a loud failure.

docs.title: Identity on the platform
docs.text:
The primary variant deploys under the bare Sigma UUID and the bare rule title, which is exactly what droid did before variants existed. Nothing already deployed moves, and no migration is needed.

Every other variant derives a stable identity from the Sigma id and its own name.

Variant Microsoft Sentinel and XDR rule_id Splunk saved search name primary the Sigma id Suspicious process edr uuid5(sigma_id, "edr") Suspicious process [edr]

The derived UUID is a function of the Sigma id and the variant name only, so it is stable across runs and unique per rule. Two different rules never collide on the same variant name.

docs.title: Platform-wide telemetry
docs.text:
A single-tenant deployment that only carries some of the declared sources can narrow them once, on the platform itself.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk]

variants = ["edr"]

Only those variants are ever converted or deployed. Omit the key to get all of them, which is the default. It narrows exactly what a per-customer list narrows, as described below.

docs.title: Per-customer telemetry
docs.text:
Customers rarely carry every source. In MSSP mode, each export_list_mssp entry may declare the variants that customer actually has.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.microsoft_xdr.export_list_mssp.Zoidberg]

tenant_id = "122d2a69-c233-4824-a009-a431d839d799"
customer_name = "Zoidberg"
customer_filters_directory = "filters/zoidberg/"
variants = ["defender", "edr"]

[platforms.microsoft_xdr.export_list_mssp.Slurm]

tenant_id = "0e3a2b3f-9c26-4b91-9f7e-30c30e9bb7a1"
customer_name = "Slurm"
variants = ["edr"]

Slurm is never sent the native Defender query, which would run against data they do not have and would silently return nothing forever.

An entry without a variants key receives every variant, which is what configurations predating this feature expect.

docs.title: What an allowlist does and does not narrow
docs.text:
One variants list covers the whole platform, so it can only narrow the log sources that actually offer a choice. A pipeline group is subject to the allowlists only if it declares a variant name.

Nearly every log source is served by a single group with no variant key. Those rules keep deploying to everyone regardless of the allowlist. Were it otherwise, adding variants to one customer to pick their process_creation source would silently stop every other rule in the repository from reaching them.

Tip

That also gives you the escape hatch for the opposite case. To withhold a single-source log source from a customer, give its pipeline group a variant name and leave that name out of their list.

You can preview the result before exporting anything. droid rules convert --mssp renders the same narrowing, so what you see per customer is what will be deployed to them.

droid --debug rules convert \
--rules rules/rules/sigma/ \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform microsoft_xdr \
--mssp
Note

Run the command with --debug to see the [customer / variant] labels. Without it the queries are printed unlabelled.

docs.title: Orphan reporting
docs.text:
Removing a variant from a customer's variants list stops droid deploying it, but whatever was already pushed keeps running in their tenant or workspace. When droid skips a customer for that reason it looks the rule up, and warns if it is still there.

Orphan rule foo.yml (defender) still deployed in tenant <id> for 'Slurm',
which no longer carries that telemetry. Remove it manually if it is no longer wanted.

droid never deletes it. Only the operator knows whether the leftover is stale or still wanted, and a detection deleted by surprise is worse than one that is merely reported.

Warning

droid can only report a variant it still knows about. Deleting a pipeline group from the configuration entirely leaves droid with no name to look up. Remove the variant from every customer's variants list first, let a run report the leftovers, and only then drop the group.

docs.title: Splunk
docs.text:
Splunk has no MSSP concept. Customers are scoped inside the query itself, by the index and splunk_server conditions the pipeline injects. A variant is therefore one saved search, with every relevant customer index merged in its pipeline. The number of saved searches is rules x variants, independent of how many customers there are.

splunk_process_creation_edr.yml
name: Splunk EDR process creation
priority: 100

transformations:
  - id: index_condition
    type: add_condition
    conditions:
      index: edr_zoidberg,edr_slurm
      splunk_server: "*prod.planet-express.local"
    rule_conditions:
      - type: logsource
        category: process_creation
        product: windows

docs.title: Suppression fields
docs.text:
Suppression fields are named per log source, but variants have different schemas. Suppressing a Sysmon rule on Computer says nothing about the same detection over EDR data, so a variant group may declare its own.

droid_config.toml
[platforms.splunk.pipelines.windows_process_creation_edr]

pipelines = ["splunk_windows", "pipelines/splunk_process_creation_edr.yml"]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"
variant = "edr"
"alert.suppress.fields" = "agent_id,process_path"

This takes precedence over the log source wide savedsearch_parameters.suppress_fields_groups entry. A variant that shares the primary's schema simply omits the key and inherits it.

Resolution semantics

For a given rule, the effective suppression fields are resolved as follows:

  • the rule's own custom: alert.suppress.fields field, if set
  • else the alert.suppress.fields of the variant's pipeline group, if set
  • else the matching savedsearch_parameters.suppress_fields_groups entry, if any
  • else the platform wide savedsearch_parameters."alert.suppress.fields", if set

docs.title: Raw rules
docs.text: droid allows the usage of a plain SIEM/EDR query instead of Sigma in the detection field. This feature was implemented to make the use of a platform's advanced search while keeping Sigma's metadata.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
First, decide where these rules will remain. For instance, these rules can remain at the following path: rules/raw. If you have multiple SIEM/EDR, you can create a subdirectory to split the rules by platform, for instance: rules/raw/siem1.

Finally, set the path in your configuration file. droid will use the argument -r and check if the path matches

droid_config.toml
[base]

raw_rules_directory = "rules/raw"

sigma_validation_config = "validation/validate.yml"
Note

In the above example base configuration file, if we're using droid rules integrity -r rules/raw/splunk -c droid_config.toml -p splunk droid will match rules/raw and will enable the raw rules features.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
To use a plain SIEM/EDR search query, just replace the Sigma's detection field as the following:

detect_web_rdmn.yml
title: Detect Suspicious Web Activities
id: 1b3b4d57-117b-4635-96a7-7d0d2c1e54b9
status: experimental
description: |
  This Sigma rule detects suspicious web activities by matching web logs against a lookup table of suspicious IPs, user agents, and URLs.
author: Apache25
date: 2024/04/05
logsource:
  product: web
  service: apache
detection: |-
  index=web_logs sourcetype=access_combined
  | lookup suspicious_activities.csv suspicious_ip AS clientip OUTPUT suspicious_ip
  | lookup suspicious_activities.csv suspicious_user_agent AS useragent OUTPUT suspicious_user_agent
  | lookup suspicious_activities.csv suspicious_url AS uri_path OUTPUT suspicious_url
  | eval is_suspicious_ip=if(isnotnull(suspicious_ip), 1, 0)
  | eval is_suspicious_user_agent=if(isnotnull(suspicious_user_agent), 1, 0)
  | eval is_suspicious_url=if(isnotnull(suspicious_url), 1, 0)
  | eval total_suspicious_score=is_suspicious_ip + is_suspicious_user_agent + is_suspicious_url
  | where total_suspicious_score > 0
  | eval suspicious_reason=case(
      is_suspicious_ip==1, "Suspicious IP",
      is_suspicious_user_agent==1, "Suspicious User Agent",
      is_suspicious_url==1, "Suspicious URL",
      total_suspicious_score==2, "Multiple Indicators",
      total_suspicious_score==3, "Highly Suspicious"
    )
  | stats count BY clientip, useragent, uri_path, suspicious_reason
  | sort -count
  | rename clientip AS "Client IP", useragent AS "User Agent", uri_path AS "URL Path", suspicious_reason AS "Reason"
  | fields "Client IP", "User Agent", "URL Path", "Reason", count
  | eval action_required=case(
      count > 10, "Immediate Action",
      count > 5, "Review Required",
      count <= 5, "Monitor"
    )
  | sort -action_required
  | table "Client IP", "User Agent", "URL Path", "Reason", count, action_required
  | rename count AS "Suspicious Activity Count"
fields:
  - clientip
  - useragent
  - uri_path
  - suspicious_reason
  - count
  - action_required
falsepositives:
  - Known internal tests
  - False positives due to misconfiguration
level: high
Info

When using the raw rules the features to validate and convert the rules will be possible. Currently, droid does not support any custom validation rule for the raw rules. However, when using droid in a CI/CD pipeline workflow, you can run another script of your own to validate these rules.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
droid is able to:

  • Validate the content of the rules
  • Convert the Sigma rules
  • Perform ad-hoc search on the platform and report for findings
  • Export (deploy) the rules
  • Check the integrity of the rules on platforms
Note

droid is a command line tool using subcommands.

  • Commands are grouped under droid rules or droid sources
  • Make sure to specify the droid configuration file using -c
  • You can select a directory (this will load all the rules within sub-directories) or a single rule
  • You can generate a JSON logging file using -j (global option, placed before the subcommand)
  • Debug mode is enabled with -d or --debug (global option, placed before the subcommand)

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
Note

This requires a validation configuration, see here.

droid rules validate \
--rules sigma/sigmahq-core/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_wmic_susp_process_creation.yml \
--config-file droid_config.toml

docs.title: Convert
docs.text:
droid rules convert \
--rules rules/sigma/ \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform splunk

With debug output:

droid --debug rules convert \
--rules rules/sigma/ \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform splunk
Info

If you want to use the Sigma filters, you can store your filters in a directory and use the sigma_filters_directory parameter. See the configuration.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Note

This features works only with the supported platforms.

Info

droid will report for findings as per the configured search timerange in your configuration. If there is any hit, it will raise a warning but not an error exit-code.

droid rules search \
--rules sigma/sigmahq-core/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_wmic_susp_process_creation.yml \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform microsoft_sentinel

You can use the search feature to use Microsoft XDR converted rules with Microsoft Sentinel as a search head. This will use your Microsoft Sentinel setup to search. It's also compatible with the --mssp mode.

droid rules search \
--rules sigma/sigmahq-core/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_wmic_susp_process_creation.yml \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform microsoft_xdr \
--sentinel-xdr

docs.title: MSSP
docs.text:
Currently the MSSP mode is available for Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft XDR.

droid rules search \
--rules sigma/sigmahq-core/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_wmic_susp_process_creation.yml \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform microsoft_sentinel \
--mssp

When using the MSSP mode, you have the ability to apply specific filters for designated customers. By adding customer_name and customers_filters_directory in the TOML configuration in platforms.<platform>.export_list_mssp.CustomerName, droid will add the default filters directory from base AND the Sigma filters in customer_filters_directory.

Example:

            [platforms.microsoft_xdr.export_list_mssp.Zoidberg]

            tenant_id = "122d2a69-c233-4824-a009-a431d839d799"
            customer_name = "Zoidberg"
            customer_filters_directory = "filters/zoidberg/"

Customers do not always carry the same telemetry. When a log source is served by several sources, the variants key of an export_list_mssp entry selects the ones a given customer has, so they only receive the queries their data can answer. See log source variants.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Info

If you have set one or multiple rule with any of the custom field disabled or removed as True, droid will make sure it is set as disabled or remove the detection rule if it exists on the platform.

droid --debug rules export \
--rules rules/rules/sigma/ \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform splunk

docs.title: Integrity
docs.text:
Info

This feature verify if the id, description and rule search match the platform's saved search.

droid --debug rules integrity \
--rules rules/rules/sigma/ \
--config-file droid_config.toml \
--platform splunk

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
The following platforms are supported:

  • Splunk
  • Elastic Security
  • Microsoft Sentinel
  • Microsoft XDR
Info

If the platform you are using is missing, feel free to contribute to the project.

docs.text:

    • Remove detection rules
    • Disable detection rules
  • Detection rule actions
    • Index
    • Server log
    • Email
    • Webhook

docs.title: Index detection
docs.text:
Warning

It is necessary to specify the indexes within the Sigma pipeline or it will be defaulted to logs-*.

docs.title: Data streams
docs.text:
Most logs live in data streams, named <type>-<dataset>-<namespace>. Point the pipeline at the data stream, never at its backing indices: a document showing "_index": ".ds-logs-vault-planet.express-2026.10.29-000034" belongs to the data stream logs-vault-planet.express. Elasticsearch prefixes the backing indices with .ds-, suffixes them with a date and a generation, and rolls them over.

val Matches logs-vault-planet.express that data stream only logs-*-planet.express every dataset of the planet.express namespace logs-vault-* the vault dataset in every namespace *-vault-planet.express-* nothing: the name ends with the namespace, there is no - after

Wildcards skip the hidden .ds- backing indices unless the pattern itself starts with a ..

When several sources share one dataset, e.g. a generic fallback one, the index cannot tell them apart: add a condition on a field that does, with an add_condition transformation in the same pipeline.

Before deploying, check what a pattern resolves to:

GET _resolve/index/logs-*-planet.express
Single indexMultiple index 
name: Elastic Windows Process Creation
priority: 100

transformations:

- id: index_set_state
  type: set_state
  key: "index"
  val: "windows-sysmon.*"
  rule_conditions:
    - type: logsource
      product: windows
      category: process_creation

name: Elastic Windows Process Creation
priority: 100

transformations:

- id: index_set_state
  type: set_state
  key: "index"
  val:
    - "windows-sysmon.*"
    - "windows-sysmon2.*"
  rule_conditions:
    - type: logsource
      product: windows
      category: process_creation

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The same credentials are used for Kibana (export and integrity) and for Elasticsearch (search). Set auth_method to one of:

  • basic: Authenticate using username and password, loaded from the environment variables:
    • DROID_ELASTIC_USERNAME : Elastic username
    • DROID_ELASTIC_PASSWORD : Elastic password
  • api_key: Authenticate using an Elasticsearch API key, loaded from the environment variable:
    • DROID_ELASTIC_API_KEY : the encoded API key, as returned in the encoded field when the key is created
[platforms.elastic]
auth_method = "api_key"

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Give droid a user, or an API key, of its own with the least privileges. Kibana runs a detection rule with the API key of whoever saved it last: the rules droid exports read the source indices with droid's privileges, not with the ones of an analyst.

Privilege Kind Needed by read on the indices the rules read Elasticsearch search, and every run of the exported rules Security > Rules and Exceptions: All Kibana export (create, update, remove) and integrity Management > Actions and Connectors: Read Kibana export, only when rule actions are configured

No cluster privilege is needed, nor any privilege on the alerts index: Kibana writes the alerts itself. As a role, in the space the rules go to:

PUT _security/role/droid
{
  "cluster": [],
  "indices": [
    {"names": ["logs-*"], "privileges": ["read"]}
  ],
  "applications": [
    {
      "application": "kibana-.kibana",
      "privileges": ["feature_securitySolutionRulesV4.all", "feature_actions.read"],
      "resources": ["space:default"]
    }
  ]
}
Note
  • List in indices every index pattern of your pipelines. A rule reading an index droid cannot read runs, but finds nothing.
  • The Kibana feature names carry a version, securitySolutionRulesV4 on Kibana 9.5. GET kbn:/api/features lists the ones of your Kibana, or pick Rules and Exceptions in Stack Management > Roles.
  • For an API key, create it as an administrator with the role above in its role_descriptors. A user creating its own API keys needs the manage_own_api_key cluster privilege on top.

docs.title: Kibana spaces
docs.text:
Droid exports to the default space, or to the space of your choice, e.g. one per team:

[platforms.elastic]
kibana_url = "https://kibana.planet-express.local"
space = "planet-express" # (1)!
  1. The ID of the space, as in its URLs /s/planet-express/app/..., not its name.

Export, integrity and removal then only see the rules of that space: a rule of the same ID in another space is another rule. Searches run on Elasticsearch, which has no spaces.

Warning
  • The connectors of the rule actions must exist in that space. Connector IDs are unique across all the spaces of Kibana while a connector is only usable in its own, so give each space's connectors IDs of their own, e.g. planet-express-alerts-index.
  • Grant the privileges in that space: "resources": ["space:planet-express"].

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
For Sigma rules both esql (ES|QL) and eql (EQL) are supported. ES|QL supports every correlation type EQL does and more, see Correlation rules, and there are no known benefits to using EQL over ES|QL.

For raw rules, both esql (ES|QL) and eql (EQL) are supported. Always use the raw_language custom field to specify the language used in the Sigma yaml file.

For non correlation ES|QL rules, the metadata fields are automatically added to the query for better deduplication by the Elastic backend. Correlation ES|QL rules aggregate their events and have no _id to deduplicate on, droid suppresses their repeated alerts instead, see Correlation rules.

docs.title: Query format
docs.text:
Converted ES|QL queries read like the ones written in Kibana: the source command first, then one upper-case command per line.

FROM logs-endpoint.events.process-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE process.name=="powershell.exe" AND `1vendor.process.args` LIKE "*-enc*"

ES|QL and EQL only accept a field name without backticks when every segment of it starts with a letter (or with _ or @) and is not a reserved word. Droid quotes every other field name for you, which covers:

  • a segment starting with a digit, e.g. a vendor prefix like 1vendor.category
  • a segment that is a reserved word, e.g. delivery.by or rule.first in ES|QL, rule.sequence in EQL
  • any character outside letters, digits and _, e.g. process.parent-name
Note

Upgrading to a version of droid that changes the query format updates every deployed rule on the next export, and reports an integrity mismatch for each rule until it is exported again.

docs.title: MITRE ATT&CK
docs.text:
The attack.* tags of a rule fill its MITRE ATT&CK mapping in Kibana:

  • a technique is listed under every tactic it belongs to, e.g. attack.t1078 under Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation and Stealth
  • a subtechnique is nested under its technique, e.g. attack.t1078.004
  • a tactic tag without technique, e.g. attack.initial-access or attack.ta0001, keeps its own entry

The other tags are exported as Kibana tags.

docs.title: Severity and risk score
docs.text:
Sigma level Severity Risk score critical critical 99 high high 73 medium medium 47 low low 21 informational low 1

Elastic has no informational severity, the risk score keeps those rules apart from the low ones.

docs.title: Correlation rules
docs.text:
Correlation rules are supported with ES|QL, and partly with EQL. Write the correlation and the rules it references in one file:

title: Vault Sign-In Failure
name: vault_signin_failure
# ...
logsource:
    product: vault
    service: signin_attempts
detection:
    selection:
        category: credentials_failed
    condition: selection
---
title: Vault Brute Force
# ...
correlation:
    type: event_count
    rules:
        - vault_signin_failure
    group-by:
        - target_user.email
    timespan: 10m
    condition:
        gte: 5

which converts to:

FROM logs-signin-attempts-planet-express-default METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE `1vault.signinattempts.category`=="credentials_failed"
| EVAL timebucket=date_trunc(10minutes, @timestamp)
| STATS event_count=count() BY timebucket, `1vault.signinattempts.target_user.email`
| WHERE event_count >= 5
Correlation type ES|QL EQL event_count Yes With a gte condition only, as a sequence ... with runs=N value_count Yes No temporal Yes Yes, as a sample temporal_ordered No No

Droid warns and skips a correlation the language cannot express. On EQL, the backend would render value_count as a sequence of events sharing the counted value, the opposite of distinct values, any event_count condition as "at least", and temporal_ordered as a query Elasticsearch cannot parse.

An EQL sequence counts the events within its maxspan, a sliding window, where ES|QL counts them per time bucket. Kibana deduplicates the alerts of EQL correlations itself, the suppression of repeated alerts is only needed by ES|QL. An EQL sample has no time window: the look-back of the rule bounds it.

Only the correlation is deployed: the rules it references are part of its query, and a rule of the file it does not reference is not deployed either.

docs.title: Pipelines for correlations
docs.text:
A log source group can convert its correlation rules with other pipelines through pipelines_correlation, see Correlation rule overrides. The whole file is then converted with these pipelines, including the rules the correlation references, so the list must still hold the field mappings and conditions of these rules. A typical use is pointing the aggregation at a narrower index:

[platforms.elastic.pipelines.vault_signin_attempts]
pipelines = ["pipelines/elastic_vault.yml"]
pipelines_correlation = [
    "pipelines/elastic_vault.yml",
    "pipelines/elastic_vault_correlation.yml", # (1)!
]
product = "vault"
service = "signin_attempts"
  1. A higher priority pipeline that sets the index state to the sign-in data stream alone.

docs.title: Look-back
docs.text: Kibana only hands a rule the events between from and the time it runs. A correlation looks back over its timespan on top of the schedule interval and the additional_look_back: a 1 hour correlation scheduled every 5 minutes runs with from: now-3900s.

docs.title: Suppression of repeated alerts
docs.text:
Each run within the look-back sees the same group again, and Kibana would raise a new alert for it every time. Unless an alert suppression is configured for the rule, droid suppresses the alerts of a correlation on timebucket and its group-by fields, for the duration of the look-back: the runs that follow add to the first alert instead of raising new ones.

Warning
  • Alert suppression needs a Platinum license or higher. On a lower license, set suppress_correlation_alerts = false, and expect one alert per run for as long as a group stays within the look-back.
  • Kibana suppresses on three fields at most: a correlation grouped by more than two fields is deployed without suppression, with a warning, until you pick its fields with an alert suppression.

docs.title: Time buckets
docs.text: The correlation counts events per fixed timespan bucket (date_trunc), not over a sliding window. With a 10 minutes timespan, five failures between 09:08 and 09:12 fall in two buckets, 09:00 and 09:10, and do not match a gte: 5 condition.

docs.title: Alert suppression
docs.text:
A noisy rule raises one alert per matching event. Alert suppression raises one alert per group of field values instead, e.g. one per account and per hour: the events that follow are counted on that alert, in kibana.alert.suppression.docs_count, and run no action. It is the counterpart of alert.suppress.fields and alert.suppress.period on Splunk.

Warning

Alert suppression needs a Platinum license or higher.

Parameter Mandatory Default Description group_by Yes N/A 1 to 3 fields, as named in Elasticsearch once the pipelines mapped them duration No None Suppress for this period, e.g. 90s, 30m or 4h. Without it, alerts are only grouped within each rule run missing_fields No suppress suppress groups the events missing a group_by field together, do_not_suppress alerts on each of them

A rule takes the first suppression found among:

  1. its custom field elastic_suppression, false turning suppression off for the rule
  2. the suppression of its pipeline group, each variant having its own
  3. the [platforms.elastic.suppression] of the platform
RulePipeline groupPlatform 
custom:
    elastic_suppression:
        group_by:
            - 1vault.signinattempts.target_user.email
        duration: 1h

[platforms.elastic.pipelines.vault_signin_attempts]
pipelines = ["pipelines/elastic_vault.yml"]
product = "vault"
service = "signin_attempts"
suppression = { group_by = ["1vault.signinattempts.target_user.email"], duration = "1h" }

[platforms.elastic.suppression]
group_by = ["host.name"]
duration = "4h"

A suppression configured for a correlation replaces the one droid sets on its own. Its fields can only be among the ones the correlation returns, timebucket and its group-by fields, droid warns about any other. Without duration, the correlation is suppressed over its look-back.

docs.title: Alerts per run
docs.text: A rule run raises at most max_signals alerts, 100 by default. Kibana drops the others and flags the run with a warning. Raise it for the platform with max_signals, or for one rule with the custom field elastic_max_signals. Kibana caps it with xpack.alerting.rules.run.alerts.max, 1000 by default.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
A rule runs every interval and looks back over that interval, plus the additional_look_back, plus the timespan of a correlation. A rare, expensive rule can run hourly while a critical one runs every minute, each taking the first value found among:

Level Interval Additional look-back Rule custom field elastic_interval custom field elastic_additional_look_back Pipeline group interval additional_look_back Platform schedule_interval and schedule_interval_unit additional_look_back

Durations are written like 90s, 5m, 1h or 1d.

RulePipeline group 
custom:
    elastic_interval: 1h
    elastic_additional_look_back: 5m # (1)!
  1. Every run covers the last 65 minutes.
[platforms.elastic.pipelines.windows_driver_load]
pipelines = ["pipelines/elastic_windows.yml"]
product = "windows"
category = "driver_load"
interval = "15m"

docs.title: Export and integrity
docs.text:
Export creates the rules missing from Kibana and updates the ones that differ from what droid would deploy, leaving the others untouched: running it again over unchanged rules changes nothing. A rule whose language changed, from ES|QL to EQL or back, is deleted and created again. The custom fields disabled, building_block and removed disable the rule, make it a building block, or delete it; deleting a rule already gone is not an error.

Integrity checks that each rule on Kibana is the one export would deploy, field by field, and names every field that differs:

  • the query, and the index of EQL rules
  • the name, description, severity, risk score, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and tags
  • the schedule and look-back, interval and from
  • the actions, alert suppression and max_signals
  • whether the rule is enabled, and whether it is a building block

A rule changed on Kibana since its export, or changed in the repository and not exported yet, fails the check. So does a rule marked removed still on Kibana, or a rule Kibana cannot show droid.

docs.title: Rule actions
docs.text:
Rule actions notify, or keep track, when a rule raises alerts. Each action runs a Kibana connector: droid attaches the actions to the rules it exports, the connectors themselves are created in Kibana beforehand, since they hold the secrets (SMTP password, webhook credentials).

Type Connector Minimum license Default frequency index .index Basic For each alert server_log .server-log Basic Summary per run email .email Gold Summary per run webhook .webhook Gold Summary per run

Declare each action under [platforms.elastic.actions.<name>]. A global action, the default, runs on every rule that does not select its own with the custom field elastic_actions; set global = false to run it only on the rules that name it, see Opt-in actions.

[platforms.elastic.actions.alerts_index]
type = "index"
connector_id = "droid-alerts-index" # (1)!

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_email]
type = "email"
connector_id = "planet-express-smtp"
to = ["leela@planet-express.local"]
cc = ["hermes@planet-express.local"]
throttle = "1h" # (2)!

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_webhook]
type = "webhook"
connector_id = "planet-express-dispatch"
  1. The ID of the connector in Kibana, as shown in Stack Management > Connectors or returned when the connector is created.
  2. At most one summary per hour, however often the rule runs.
custom:
    elastic_actions:
        - dispatch_email # (1)!
  1. This rule only sends the email. elastic_actions: [] runs no action at all.

docs.title: Opt-in actions
docs.text:
An action with global = false runs only on the rules that name it, not on every rule that selects none. Use it when an action belongs to a few rules, e.g. one email per team, instead of firing for every rule the platform exports:

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_email]
type = "email"
connector_id = "planet-express-smtp"
to = ["leela@planet-express.local"]
global = false # (1)!
  1. Opt-in: it runs on the rules naming it, and a rule selecting nothing does not send it.
custom:
    elastic_actions:
        - dispatch_email # (1)!
  1. A rule names the action to run it, and may still override its parameters.

A non-global action is built and checked as usual, its connector_id and parameters included: opting in only decides which rules run it, it is not a switch that skips an action left without its parameters.

docs.title: Overrides per rule
docs.text:
A rule can also change the parameters of its actions, e.g. to reach another team, by mapping each action to the parameters it overrides. The others come from the configuration:

custom:
    elastic_actions:
        dispatch_email: # (1)!
            to:
                - zoidberg@planet-express.local
            subject: "Claws out: {{context.rule.name}}"
        alerts_index: # (2)!
  1. Sent to Zoidberg, still with Hermes in cc as configured.
  2. Selected without any change.

Rule files are usually open to more people than the configuration, and an action sends what the rule found. A rule therefore only overrides what its action lets it, listed in overridable: nothing by default. An email action can also bind the recipients rules give it to some domains:

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_email]
type = "email"
connector_id = "planet-express-smtp"
to = ["leela@planet-express.local"]
cc = ["hermes@planet-express.local"]
overridable = ["to", "subject"] # (1)!
allowed_recipient_domains = ["planet-express.local"] # (2)!
  1. Any parameter of the action, per_alert, throttle and connector_id can be listed, never its type.
  2. Only binds the recipients a rule gives: to = ["mom@momcorp.example"] in a rule fails its export, while the configuration stays free to send outside. Each recipient a rule gives must be a single plain address: an entry hiding several, such as "mom@momcorp.example, leela@planet-express.local", is refused.

A rule overriding anything else fails its export, naming the parameter, and nothing of it is deployed.

Webhook per rule

Splunk sets the webhook URL of a rule. On Kibana, the URL belongs to the connector, along with its credentials: create a webhook connector per target, and let the rules pick theirs.

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_webhook]
type = "webhook"
connector_id = "planet-express-dispatch"
overridable = ["connector_id"]

custom:
    elastic_actions:
        dispatch_webhook:
            connector_id: momcorp-dispatch

Kibana refuses a connector of another type, a rule cannot turn its webhook into an email.

docs.title: Common parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Mandatory Default Description type Yes N/A index, server_log, email or webhook connector_id Yes N/A ID of the Kibana connector the action runs per_alert No Depends on the type true runs the action for each alert, false once per rule run with a summary of its alerts throttle No None Summary only: run at most once per period, e.g. "1h", instead of on each rule run with alerts overridable No [] Parameters a rule may override allowed_recipient_domains No None Email only: domains the recipients a rule gives must belong to global No true false makes the action opt-in: it runs only on the rules naming it

Any other parameter is rejected, a typo fails before anything is exported.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
Keeps the alerts in an index of your own, e.g. to archive them longer than the alerts index or to feed another tool. By default each alert is indexed whole, under alert, with the rule, the reason and the source event:

{
  "@timestamp": "2026-11-07T18:06:45.917Z",
  "alert": {
    "kibana": {"alert": {"rule": {"name": "Vault Brute Force", "...": "..."}, "reason": "...", "severity": "medium"}},
    "1vault": {"signinattempts": {"target_user": {"email": "kif@planet-express.local"}}}
  }
}

With per_alert = false, a single document per run holds rule_id, rule_name, severity, risk_score, alerts_count and results_link. Replace the document with document, a table whose values can use the action variables:

[platforms.elastic.actions.alerts_index]
type = "index"
connector_id = "droid-alerts-index"
document = { rule = "{{context.rule.name}}", alert_id = "{{alert.id}}" }

Create the index and its connector before exporting. Alerts hold hundreds of fields, the flattened type keeps them searchable without hitting the field limit of the index:

PUT planet-express-alerts
{
  "mappings": {
    "properties": {
      "@timestamp": {"type": "date"},
      "alert": {"type": "flattened"}
    }
  }
}

POST kbn:/api/actions/connector/droid-alerts-index
{
  "name": "Alerts archive",
  "connector_type_id": ".index",
  "config": {"index": "planet-express-alerts", "refresh": false, "executionTimeField": "@timestamp"}
}
Warning

A document given as a string is not JSON escaped by Kibana: a rule name holding a quote turns it into invalid JSON, and the action fails in the Kibana logs only. Prefer a table, whose values are escaped.

docs.title: Server log
docs.text:
Writes a line in the Kibana log, handy to check that actions run. level is one of trace, debug, info (default), warn, error or fatal, and message replaces the default line.

[platforms.elastic.actions.kitchen_log]
type = "server_log"
connector_id = "droid-server-log"
level = "warn"

POST kbn:/api/actions/connector/droid-server-log
{"name": "Server log", "connector_type_id": ".server-log"}

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
Sends the alerts by email. At least one of to, cc or bcc is required. subject and message (Markdown) replace the defaults, which give the rule, its severity and risk score, the number of alerts and a link to them.

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_email]
type = "email"
connector_id = "planet-express-smtp"
to = ["leela@planet-express.local"]
subject = "[{{context.rule.severity}}] {{context.rule.name}}"

POST kbn:/api/actions/connector/planet-express-smtp
{
  "name": "Planet Express SMTP",
  "connector_type_id": ".email",
  "config": {"service": "other", "host": "smtp.planet-express.local", "port": 587, "secure": false, "from": "droid@planet-express.local"},
  "secrets": {"user": "droid", "password": "..."}
}

See the email connector for the other services (Exchange, Outlook, ...).

Note

Kibana escapes the Markdown characters of the variables in the message. The HTML part of the email reads as expected, while a text-only mail client shows the escapes, e.g. PIZZA \- Vault Brute Force.

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
Posts the alerts as JSON, e.g. to a SOAR. body replaces the default:

Summary (default)per_alert = true 
{"rule_id": "…", "rule_name": "…", "severity": "…", "risk_score": 47, "results_link": "…", "alerts_count": 2, "alerts": [{…}, {…}]}

{"rule_id": "…", "rule_name": "…", "severity": "…", "risk_score": 47, "results_link": "…", "alert": {…}}

[platforms.elastic.actions.dispatch_webhook]
type = "webhook"
connector_id = "planet-express-dispatch"
per_alert = true

POST kbn:/api/actions/connector/planet-express-dispatch
{
  "name": "Planet Express dispatch",
  "connector_type_id": ".webhook",
  "config": {"url": "https://soar.planet-express.local/hooks/droid", "method": "post", "hasAuth": true, "authType": "webhook-authentication-basic"},
  "secrets": {"user": "droid", "password": "..."}
}

In the body, {{ }} values are JSON escaped by Kibana and {{{ }}} are inserted raw, which is how the alerts go in as JSON objects.

docs.title: Action variables
docs.text:
Templates use the Security rule action variables, among them:

Variable Value {{context.rule.name}} Name of the rule, with its alert_prefix {{context.rule.rule_id}} ID of the Sigma rule {{context.rule.severity}} Severity of the rule {{context.rule.risk_score}} Risk score of the rule {{context.rule.description}} Description of the rule {{state.signals_count}} Number of alerts of the run {{context.alerts}} The alerts, as JSON: the one alert of a per alert action {{alert.id}} ID of the alert, per alert actions only {{context.results_link}} Link to the alerts in Kibana {{date}} Time of the run Note

context.results_link stays empty until server.publicBaseUrl is set in the Kibana configuration.

docs.title: Sigma Custom Fields
docs.text:
The Custom Fields available with the Elastic Integration are:

docs.text:
Two authentication mode are supported:

  • default: Default authentication via az login
  • app: Azure Registration App

When using the default authentication:

  1. Head to portal.azure.com and authenticate using MFA
  2. Use az cli to fetch the authentication session

When using the Azure Registation App, load the following environment variables:

  • DROID_AZURE_TENANT_ID: Azure tenant ID
  • DROID_AZURE_CLIENT_ID: Client ID of the registration app
  • DROID_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET: Azure client secret

The keys workspace_id, workspace_name, subscription_id and resource_group are the base workspace declaration but they can be replaced with the following environment variables:

  • DROID_AZURE_WORKSPACE_ID
  • DROID_AZURE_WORKSPACE_NAME
  • DROID_AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
  • DROID_AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
Note

The authentication method can be provided using the environment variables DROID_AZURE_SEARCH_AUTH and DROID_AZURE_EXPORT_AUTH. This will override the parameters search_auth and export_auth from the TOML configuration.

Warning

On Microsoft Sentinel, search_auth is used for both searches and exports: export_auth is not read.

Custom authentication via hook:

We have also added the ability retrieve Azure Tokens from any custom app via a hook.

If the environment variable DROID_AZURE_TOKEN_HOOK is set with a URL, the hook attempts to acquire the token from that URL via a GET request. The response should contain a JSON object with the access_token key, which will be used as the token.

The hook function supports dynamic URL configuration using placeholders:

  • {TENANT_ID}: Replaced with the provided or default tenant ID.
  • {SCOPE}: Replaced with the requested scope.

Additional infos:

  • Uses the cached token if it is still valid and the scope matches.
  • Supports retries for token retrieval, with retry count and delay.
  • If DROID_AZURE_TOKEN_X_API_KEY environment variable is present, it will be included in the request headers.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
A rule is deployed as a scheduled rule, unless it asks to be a near real-time rule.

Scheduled rules run every query_frequency hours and search the last query_period hours of data. An alert is raised when the number of results compares to threshold_value as threshold_operator says: GreaterThan and 0 raise an alert on the first result. A rule overrides both values with custom.query_frequency and custom.query_period.

Logs reach the workspace some minutes after they happen, more for some sources. With a query_period equal to query_frequency, an event that arrives after the run covering it never matches: a run only looks at its own window. A query_period longer than query_frequency, such as 2 and 1, catches it on the next run. The overlap has a cost: an event already ingested in time matches both runs, and raises two alerts. Incident grouping puts the second alert in the incident of the first, as long as the incident is still open and the entities match.

Near real-time (NRT) rules run about every minute on the data ingested since their last run, so they neither miss late events nor raise duplicates. A rule is deployed as NRT with query_period: 0, the value which also makes it near real-time on Microsoft XDR:

...
custom:
  query_period: 0

An NRT rule has no frequency, lookback or threshold: query_frequency, query_period, threshold_operator and threshold_value do not apply, and every result raises an alert. Suppression, incident creation, grouping and entity mappings apply as for a scheduled rule.

Warning

Microsoft Sentinel allows 50 NRT rules per workspace. Keep them for the rules where minutes matter, such as a sign-in with a break-glass account.

Note

A rule already deployed can switch between scheduled and NRT: droid deletes the deployed rule and creates it again with its new kind, as Microsoft Sentinel cannot be relied on to change it in place. If the creation fails after the deletion, droid logs that the rule is no longer deployed in that workspace. The integrity check (droid rules integrity) reports a rule deployed with the wrong kind.

docs.title: Suppression
docs.text: Suppression does not deduplicate alerts: once the rule raises an alert, Microsoft Sentinel stops running it for suppress_period hours. Any activity in that window is never searched, not even a different entity doing the same thing. Prefer incident grouping to reduce noise, and keep suppress_status for rules that need it.

docs.title: MSSP mode
docs.text:
The MSSP mode (--mssp) in Microsoft Sentinel allows to perform various operations involving multiple workspaces.

When using droid rules search, this mode allows to query multiple Microsoft Sentinel workspaces for one or multiple rules. To achieve that, droid will first list all the Microsoft Sentinel workspaces using an Azure Resource Graph query and will query all the workspaces with parallel tasks.

This mode also allows to export (droid rules export) detection rules to specific Microsoft Sentinel workspaces included in the droid configuration file.

To designate the Microsoft Sentinel workspaces, define them under the export_list_mssp section as a dictionary.

[platforms.microsoft_sentinel.export_list_mssp]

    [platforms.microsoft_sentinel.export_list_mssp.momcorp]

    workspace_name = "momcorp_sentinel"
    tenant_id = "10e5ca4d-25ac-4d17-ae8d-0314ff0d8d44"
    resource_group_name = "momcorp_resource_group_prod"
    subscription_id = "98b80a67-4fec-424c-8f06-56be08deae77"

    [platforms.microsoft_sentinel.export_list_mssp.doop]

    workspace_name = "doop_sentinel"
    tenant_id = "900b0bdf-4de1-48bb-bda4-862f638a92ac"
    resource_group_name = "doop_resource_group_prod"
    subscription_id = "94406b12-28d7-4505-9bfc-fade6ec9a560"
Note

The integrity feature (droid rules integrity) is also available.

Each entry also accepts a variants key, which selects the telemetry sources that workspace carries when a log source is served by more than one. See log source variants.

When using the search mode along with the --mssp argument you can exclude some workspaces from the search.

[platforms.microsoft_sentinel]
...
mssp_search_exclude_list = ["Foo", "Sentinel3"]

docs.title: Entity mappings
docs.text:
entity_mappings maps the columns returned by the query to the entities of the alerts. entity_type is one of the Sentinel entity types (Account, Host, IP, URL, FileHash...), and each of its field_mappings pairs an identifier of that entity with a column_name of the query. An unknown entity type, or a field mapping without its identifier or column_name, fails the export of the rule.

The integrity check (droid rules integrity) compares the entity mappings deployed with the ones of the rule, or of its log source, in any order: entities added, removed or changed on the portal are reported. A rule mapping no entities is expected to have none deployed.

docs.title: Entity mappings per log source
docs.text:
Which entities a rule returns depends on the table it queries, rather than on the rule: every rule on process creation events returns a host and an account. entity_mappings_groups maps them once for a log source, and every rule of that log source takes them, unless it sets its own entity_mappings. A group matches the rules whose logsource has exactly its product, category and service, as the pipelines do.

[platforms.microsoft_sentinel.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"

[[platforms.microsoft_sentinel.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation.entity_mappings]]
entity_type = "Host"
field_mappings = [
    { identifier = "HostName", column_name = "Computer" },
]

[[platforms.microsoft_sentinel.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation.entity_mappings]]
entity_type = "Account"
field_mappings = [
    { identifier = "FullName", column_name = "SubjectUserName" },
]

The mappings are the same as in the entity_mappings of a rule, with the Sentinel entity types rather than the Microsoft XDR ones, and must be returned by the query of every rule of the log source: check the pipelines of the log source project them. A group without mappings, or with an invalid one, fails when droid starts. A rule without a log source, such as a raw rule, takes no group.

The groups apply to every workspace of the MSSP mode, and to the Sentinel rules deployed with --sentinel-xdr, which read this same microsoft_sentinel section.

Upgrading

The rules already deployed with other entity mappings than the ones droid now expects, such as the rules of a mapped log source deployed before, are reported by the integrity check until they are exported again.

docs.title: Microsoft XDR
docs.text:
Upgrading from droid 0.4.0: Graph API changes

Microsoft removed several properties of the custom detection rules API on 2026-10-01. droid now manages the rules on Graph v1.0 with their replacements. Most rules and configurations keep working unchanged, except:

Change What to do custom.impactedAssets is no longer pushed Rules already deployed keep the entities Microsoft converted their impactedAssets into. For new rules, and to keep entities in code, move them to custom.xdr_entity_mappings, or map their log source with entity_mappings_groups. droid warns about every rule still using it isolateDevice without isolationType The isolation type was silently dropped before, it is now an error: set full or selective

Behaviour changes, without anything to do:

  • Every ATT&CK tactic tag of a rule is pushed, each with the techniques belonging to it, where only the last tactic was kept before. See MITRE ATT&CK.
  • The device groups of blockFile and the isolation type of isolateDevice are now actually pushed.
  • The first export after the upgrade may update every rule once, to the new properties.
  • New rules get droid-<Sigma rule id> as their id on the platform, Microsoft requiring an id starting with a letter. Rules already deployed keep theirs.
  • A rule Microsoft auto-disabled after repeated failures is left disabled with a warning, and reported by the integrity check.
  • The integrity check compares every setting export deploys (schedule, severity, title, tactics, actions, entity mappings), where it only compared the query, the description and the enabled state. Rules changed on the portal by hand, which passed before, are now reported. A rule the check cannot read is now a failure rather than a pass, and in MSSP mode the tenants a log source variant is not deployed to are skipped, as export skips them.
  • The entities of a rule are only deployed and checked when the rule or its log source maps them. A rule mapping neither is created with its device mapped, and keeps on the platform the entities it has, Microsoft's included. See entity mappings.
  • A rule without any ATT&CK tactic tag is deployed without tactics, with a warning, and keeps the tactics already deployed on it.
  • A rule lookup Microsoft refuses, for missing permissions for instance, is an error: a removal used to report such a rule as already removed.
  • With the default authentication, the configured tenant_id is now read.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
A deployed rule runs on its own on Microsoft XDR, at the frequency set by query_period, in the configuration, a query_period_groups entry or the rule's custom.query_period, the rule winning over its group and the group over the configuration:

query_period Runs 0 Continuously (near real-time) 1h Every hour 3h Every 3 hours 12h Every 12 hours 24h Every day

Each run searches a window of time back from now, its lookback, which Microsoft sets from the frequency. droid does not set it: Microsoft Graph accepts a lookback, but does not return it, so droid could not check the one deployed.

Note

custom.query_period is also read by Microsoft Sentinel, as a number of hours of lookback. 0 is the only value valid on both platforms: it makes the rule near real-time on both, see Microsoft Sentinel. Any other value is a number of hours on Microsoft Sentinel, and fails the export of the rule on Microsoft XDR unless it is one of those above.

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
An identifier is required for all actions, except the device actions, which always act on DeviceId. droid pushes each identifier as the advanced hunting column holding it, so the query must return that column: initiatingProcessSHA1 needs InitiatingProcessSHA1, sha1 needs SHA1, accountSid needs AccountSid, the device actions need DeviceId.

A file action can take both a SHA-1 and a SHA-256 identifier as a list, for instance identifier: [sha1, sha256]. stopAndQuarantineFile also needs DeviceId, the device the file is stopped on, and isolateDevice requires an isolation type.

Removing an action from a rule removes it from the platform on the next export. The email actions (soft or hard delete, move to Inbox, Junk or Deleted Items) have no custom field: droid leaves the ones set on the portal alone, and does not report them in the integrity check.

Action Identifier Isolation Type Device Group forceUserPasswordReset accountSid, initiatingProcessAccountSid, requestAccountSid, onPremSid disableUser accountSid, initiatingProcessAccountSid, requestAccountSid, onPremSid markUserAsCompromised accountObjectId, initiatingProcessAccountObjectId, servicePrincipalId, recipientObjectId stopAndQuarantineFile sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1 (deviceId is always added) restrictAppExecution initiateInvestigation runAntivirusScan collectInvestigationPackage isolateDevice selective, full blockFile sha256, sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1, initiatingProcessSHA256 List of Device Groups allowFile sha256, sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1, initiatingProcessSHA256 List of Device Groups Danger

Never add both "block" and "allow" files simultaneously, as this can cause significant issues.

custom:
  disabled: false
  actions:
    - action: forceUserPasswordReset
      identifier: accountSid #accountSid, initiatingProcessAccountSid
    - action: disableUser
      identifier: initiatingProcessAccountSid #accountSid, initiatingProcessAccountSid
    - action: markUserAsCompromised
      identifier: initiatingProcessAccountObjectId #accountObjectId, initiatingProcessAccountObjectId
    - action: stopAndQuarantineFile
      identifier: initiatingProcessSHA1 # sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1
    - action: restrictAppExecution
    - action: initiateInvestigation
    - action: runAntivirusScan
    - action: collectInvestigationPackage
    - action: isolateDevice
      isolationType: selective # full, selective

    ## Allow or Block file, never both!
    - action: blockFile
      deviceGroupNames:
      identifier: initiatingProcessSHA256 # sha256, sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1, initiatingProcessSHA256
    #- action: allowFile
    #  deviceGroupNames:
    #  identifier: initiatingProcessSHA256 # sha256, sha1, initiatingProcessSHA1, initiatingProcessSHA256

docs.title: MITRE ATT&CK
docs.text:
droid pushes the attack.<tactic> and attack.t<id> tags of a rule as the tactics of its alerts, sub-techniques grouped under their technique. A rule without any tactic tag is deployed without tactics, with a warning, and the tactics already deployed on it are left as they are: removing every ATT&CK tag from a rule does not remove its tactics from the platform. Microsoft refuses a technique under a tactic it does not belong to, so each technique goes under the tagged tactics it belongs to in MITRE ATT&CK, or under its own tactics when the rule tags none of them. The ATT&CK data comes from pySigma, which downloads it on first use, as for Elastic.

ATT&CK v18 split Defense Evasion into Stealth and Defense Impairment, while Microsoft and Sigma still use Defense Evasion: droid pushes those techniques under Defense Evasion. Should Microsoft still refuse a technique, its ATT&CK being older than droid's, droid deploys the rule without it and warns.

docs.title: Entity mappings
docs.text:
Entity mappings map the columns the query returns to the entities attached to the alerts, which determine how alerts are grouped into incidents and what an analyst can pivot on. They replace impactedAssets, removed by Microsoft.

The entities of a rule come from, in order:

  1. the custom field xdr_entity_mappings of the rule
  2. the entity mappings of its log source, in the configuration
  3. neither: the rule is created with its device mapped, hosts with deviceIdColumn: DeviceId, so its query must return DeviceId. After that, droid leaves its entities as they are on the platform and does not compare them.

Droid deploys and enforces the mappings of the first two like any other setting: export updates them, and the integrity check reports a rule whose entities differ. A rule of the third kind keeps whatever entities it has, including the ones Microsoft added when it converted the impactedAssets of the rules deployed before: often more than the device alone, files and processes on SHA256 for instance.

xdr_entity_mappings has the shape of the Microsoft Sentinel entity_mappings, but the Microsoft XDR vocabulary, which is why it has its own name: a rule can carry both.

Entity type Identifiers accounts aadUserIdColumn, dnsDomainColumn, nameColumn, ntDomainColumn, sidColumn, upnColumn, upnSuffixColumn amazonResources amazonResourceIdColumn azureResources resourceIdColumn cloudApplications appIdColumn, nameColumn dns domainNameColumn, hostIpAddressColumn, serverIpColumn files nameColumn, sha1Column, sha256Column googleCloudResources fullResourceNameColumn hosts deviceIdColumn, dnsDomainColumn, nameColumn, netBiosNameColumn, ntDomainColumn ips addressColumn, scopeColumn mailboxes primaryAddressColumn mailClusters queryColumn, sourceColumn mailMessages networkMessageIdColumn, recipientColumn, senderColumn, subjectColumn oAuthApplications oAuthAppIdColumn processes sha1Column, sha256Column registryValues keyColumn, valueNameColumn securityGroups distinguishedNameColumn, objectIdColumn, sidColumn urls addressColumn

Each entry becomes one entity: map the columns identifying the same account, host or file in the same entry. A rule returning two accounts, the initiating one and the target one for instance, has two accounts entries.

The mappings to start from depend on the table the rule queries:

The rule queries Map DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceFileEvents and the other Device* tables hosts: deviceIdColumn DeviceId, nameColumn DeviceName. accounts: sidColumn InitiatingProcessAccountSid, upnColumn InitiatingProcessAccountUpn. files: sha256Column SHA256, nameColumn FileName DeviceNetworkEvents The above, and ips: addressColumn RemoteIP. urls: addressColumn RemoteUrl IdentityLogonEvents, AADSignInEventsBeta accounts: upnColumn AccountUpn, sidColumn AccountSid. ips: addressColumn IPAddress EmailEvents mailboxes: primaryAddressColumn RecipientEmailAddress. mailMessages: networkMessageIdColumn NetworkMessageId, senderColumn SenderFromAddress Warning

The identity and email tables have no DeviceId: the default device mapping does not fit the rules querying them, which must set their own xdr_entity_mappings.

custom:
  xdr_entity_mappings:
    - entity_type: hosts
      field_mappings:
        - identifier: deviceIdColumn
          column_name: DeviceId
        - identifier: nameColumn
          column_name: DeviceName
    - entity_type: accounts
      field_mappings:
        - identifier: sidColumn
          column_name: InitiatingProcessAccountSid
        - identifier: upnColumn
          column_name: InitiatingProcessAccountUpn

An unknown entity type or identifier, or an entry without field mappings, fails the export of the rule. So does a mapping Microsoft refuses, with its reason:

  • a column the query does not return: Entity mappings reference the following column(s) which are not projected by the query output
  • an entity without enough columns to identify it. An account needs aadUserIdColumn, sidColumn or upnColumn, or nameColumn with ntDomainColumn, dnsDomainColumn or upnSuffixColumn: a name alone is refused.

Deleting the field from a rule gives it the mappings of its log source on the next export. Without any for its log source, the mappings deployed stay as they are: change them on the portal, or map the log source.

Note

The columns must be returned by the query. With Sigma rules using | project, or with raw rules, check that the mapped columns are part of the output.

docs.title: Entity mappings per log source
docs.text:
Which entities a rule returns depends on the table it queries, rather than on the rule: every rule on process creation events returns a device, an account and a file. entity_mappings_groups maps them once for a log source, and every rule of that log source takes them, unless it sets its own xdr_entity_mappings. A group matches the rules whose logsource has exactly its product, category and service, as query_period_groups does.

[platforms.microsoft_xdr.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation]
product = "windows"
category = "process_creation"

[[platforms.microsoft_xdr.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation.entity_mappings]]
entity_type = "hosts"
field_mappings = [
    { identifier = "deviceIdColumn", column_name = "DeviceId" },
    { identifier = "nameColumn", column_name = "DeviceName" },
]

[[platforms.microsoft_xdr.rule_parameters.entity_mappings_groups.windows_process_creation.entity_mappings]]
entity_type = "files"
field_mappings = [
    { identifier = "sha256Column", column_name = "SHA256" },
]

The mappings are the same as in xdr_entity_mappings, and must be returned by the query of every rule of the log source: check the pipelines of the log source project them. A group without mappings, or with an invalid one, fails when droid starts.

Tip

Mapping every log source puts the entities of every rule in code, reviewed and checked by the integrity check, rather than left to Microsoft.

Migrating from impactedAssets impactedAssets xdr_entity_mappings Device / deviceId hosts / deviceIdColumn: DeviceId Device / deviceName hosts / nameColumn: DeviceName Mailbox / accountUpn mailboxes / primaryAddressColumn: AccountUpn User / accountSid accounts / sidColumn: AccountSid User / accountUpn accounts / upnColumn: AccountUpn User / accountObjectId accounts / aadUserIdColumn: AccountObjectId

As impactedAssets did, droid maps the device of a new rule without entity mappings. Mappings of the rule or of its log source replace that default: include hosts in them to keep the device.

docs.title: Disabled rules
docs.text: custom.disabled sets the status of the rule. Microsoft may also auto-disable a rule that keeps failing: droid leaves it disabled with a warning rather than re-enabling it on every export, and the integrity check reports it, until it is fixed and re-enabled on the platform.

docs.text:

To use Splunk, the following sections are required:

  • [platforms.splunk]: handle the basic configuration and the SIEM settings for searches and alerts
  • [platforms.splunk.savedsearch_parameters]: saved search parameters
  • [platforms.splunk.action]: action for rules

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
droid will require the following environment variables to authenticate on Splunk:

  • DROID_SPLUNK_USER: Splunk user
  • DROID_SPLUNK_PASSWORD: Splunk user password

The following environment variables can be set:

  • DROID_SPLUNK_URL: Replace the Splunk URL parameter.
  • DROID_SPLUNK_WEBHOOK_URL: Replace the Splunk webhook URL

docs.title: Main config
docs.text:
[platforms.splunk]

url = "splunksh-dev.pizza-planet.local" # (1)!
verify_cert = true
port = "8089"

# user and password are passed in environment variable

test_earliest_time = "-24h@h" # (2)!
test_latest_time = "now" # When using `droid rules search` # (3)!
job_ttl = 86400 # (4)!
acl_update_owner = "nobody" # (5)!
acl_update_perms_read = "group1, group2" # (6)!

## For alerts
# General config

earliest_time = "-1h@h" # (7)!
latest_time = "now" # (8)!
cron_schedule = "0 * * * *"
alert_expiration = "7d"
...

  1. The hostname of Splunk, can be replace by an env variable.

  2. droid rules search: earliest time for the searches. It must be a Splunk time modifier.

  3. droid rules search: latest time for the searches. It must be a Splunk time modifier.

  4. droid rules search: Set the job TTL in seconds.

  5. droid rules search: Set the owner of the search. Useful if droid reports for findings.

  6. droid rules search: Set the groups read permissions.

  7. droid rules export: earliest time for the saved-searches. It must be a Splunk time modifier.

  8. droid rules export: latest time for the saved-searches. It must be a Splunk time modifier.

Info

DROID fetches the url of Splunk via the key url but this value can be replaced with the environment DROID_SPLUNK_URL. This is also valid for webhook URL when DROID_SPLUNK_WEBHOOK_URL exists.

docs.title: Savedsearch config
docs.text:
[platforms.splunk.savedsearch_parameters]

alert_type = "number of events"
app = "pizza_app_rules"
sharing = "app"
alert_comparator = "greater than"
alert_threshold = 0
"alert.track" = 1
allow_skew = "67%"
"alert.suppress" = 1
"alert.digest_mode" = 0 # Per result (per row)
#"alert.suppress.period" = "8h" # Optional
#"alert.suppress.fields" = "pizza_client,host" # Optional

    # [platforms.splunk.savedsearch_parameters.suppress_fields_groups.group_name]
    # Optional: define a suppress fields groups by logsource (.e.g. web)

    #[platforms.splunk.savedsearch_parameters.suppress_fields_groups.windows_image_load]

    #category = "image_load"
    #product = "windows"
Info

When a log source is served by several telemetry sources, a variant pipeline group can declare its own alert.suppress.fields, since the field names of one source rarely apply to another.

docs.text:
Using emails:

[platforms.splunk.action]

actions = "email"
"action.email.to" = "bender.rodriguez@pizza-planet.local"
"action.email.subject" = "Alert: $name$"
"action.email.message.alert" = "Description: $description$"
